newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 13.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.
- Tax defrauders shelled out more than nine million Irish pounds in 1995 after being tracked down by the Revenue Commissioners.
- Top Irish civil servants have had pay rises of up to 100 percent over the last 10 years, more than double the increase achieved by lower grades of clerical staff in government departments.
- Analysts said another rise in interest rates could be on the way as the central bank forecast a rise in inflation to 2.25 percent next year.
- Actress Helen Mirren strongly criticised the Irish Republican Army on Thursday as she attended the premiere in Dublin of the new film "Some Mothers Son' about the H-block hunger strikers.
- An Irish government survey has indicated a massive level of fraud among social welfare recipients.
- Five non-aligned republican inmates of Portlaoise prison have made a submission to the European Committee for the Prevention of Torture and Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment (CPT).

- Pay As You Earn (PAYE) workers paid 3.5 million Irish pounds in tax and pay-related social insurance (PRSI) in 1995, up 255 million Irish pounds on 1995, the Revenue Commissioners' annual report has shown.
- Inflation remained subdued over the summer lowering the prospect of another interest rate rise.
- East Digifone has called on the Irish government to move quickly to appoint an independent telecommunications regulator.
- The Campbell Bewley restaurant group may seek a stock market listing in three or four years' time.
